ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r2.claim: Ḥāra means returned; a poet compares a person to a meteor that returns to ash after shining.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p433/r2.anchor: حار: رجع، قال الشاعر: وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوئه

FARRA:v3p251/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p251/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p251/r2.claim: He thought he would not return to God, but he certainly will; balā begins the affirmative answer before the statement that God sees him.
FARRA:v3p251/r2.anchor: وقوله عز وجل: إنه ظن أن لن يحور (14) بلى (15) . أن لن يعود إلينا إلى الآخرة. بلى ليحورن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.claim: He thought he would never return or be raised; the correction says he will return, and his Lord watched him from creation onward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r2.anchor: أن لن يرجع إلينا ولن يبعث ثم قال: {بلى} {بلى} أي: ليس كما ظن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r1.claim: The worldly complacent person does not grieve for sins or wrongdoing; instead, he is pleased by them and faces a hard reckoning and sorrowful return.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r1.anchor: لا يحزن أحدهم لذنب عمله ولا لقبيح ارتكبه

NAHHAS:v5p185/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r15.claim: An and its clause together fill the two object positions.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r15.anchor: أن وما بعدها تقوم مقام المفعولين

NAHHAS:v5p185/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p185/r16.claim: He glosses the claim that the dead will not return as a denial of resurrection.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r16.anchor: وروى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس أن لن يحور قال يقول أن لن يبعث

NAHHAS:v5p185/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r17.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p185/r17.claim: He glosses it as saying that people will not return to God.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r17.anchor: وقال مجاهد أن لن يرجع إلينا

NAHHAS:v5p185/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r18.claim: The verb ḥāra yaḥūru means to return.

NAHHAS:v5p185/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r19.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NAHHAS:v5p185/r19.claim: A prophetic supplication seeks refuge from reversal after increase.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r19.anchor: وفي الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الحور بعد الكور

NAHHAS:v5p185/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r20.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p185/r20.claim: One explanation of the supplication is seeking refuge from returning to disbelief after faith.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r20.anchor: قيل معناه أعوذ بك من الرجوع إلى الكفر بعد الإيمان

NAHHAS:v5p185/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r21.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v5p185/r21.claim: Another explanation is seeking refuge from decline after increase.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r21.anchor: وقيل أعوذ بك من النقصان بعد الزيادة

TABRISI:84:13-19/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:13-19/r4.claim: He thought during earthly life that he would not return to life for judgment, so he committed sins and violated prohibitions.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r4.anchor: ظن في دار التكليف أنه لن يرجع إلى حال الحياة في الآخرة للجزاء

TABRISI:84:13-19/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r5.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:84:13-19/r5.claim: Muqatil says the man assumed he would not return to God.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: حسب أن لا يرجع إلى الله

TABRISI:84:13-19/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:13-19/r6.claim: “Indeed” corrects the false expectation: he will return and be resurrected, and God has observed him since creating him.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r6.anchor: { بلى } ليحورن وليبعثن وليس الأمر على ما ظنه

TABRISI:84:13-19/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:84:13-19/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God knew the person before creating him and knows that his return is to God.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: كان به بصيرا قبل أن يخلقه عالما بأن مرجعه إليه

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r11.claim: He assumed he would never return or undergo reversal, that his joy would not become grief, and that he would neither die nor face punishment or accountability.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r11.anchor: asla dönmeyecek, inkılâb görmeyecek sürûru kedere çevrilmeyecek, ölmeyecek

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r12.claim: Hawr is a return from completion to diminution and loss, like decline after increase, corruption after righteousness, or regression after progress.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r12.anchor: “Havr” bir kemâlden sonra noksan ve zevâle rücû‘ve inkılâbdır.

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r13.claim: A Prophetic supplication seeks refuge from decline after increase, illustrating hawr as reversal from improvement to loss.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r13.anchor: bir hadîs-i şerîfte نـَعُوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الْحَوْرِ بـَعْدَ الْكَوْرِ “kevrden sonra havrden Allah’a sığınırız”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r4.claim: They assumed they would not be raised after death and therefore pursued worldly pleasure without concern for the Hereafter, where they expect no share.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r4.anchor: The implication is that they thought that after their death

STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.claim: Joy among his people signifies worldly life and the heedlessness of disbelievers who rejected return to God and the Resurrection reckoning.
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.anchor: Among his people he was joyful refers to the life of this world; it represents the heedlessness of those who did not believe

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r1.claim: The person who receives his book behind his back thought he would not return to God or be raised after death, so he neither expected reward nor feared punishment and indulged in sins.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه ظن أن لن يحور} [الانشقاق: 14] يقول: يبعث

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r2.claim: The verb حار means to return from an affair; the cited prayer uses it for reverting to disbelief after faith.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r2.anchor: الأمر: إذا رجع عنه، ومنه الخبر الذي روي عن رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r3.claim: A prayer attributed to the Prophet seeks refuge from al-hawr after al-kawr, which al-Tabari explains as returning to disbelief after faith; no grading is stated.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r3.anchor: ومنه الخبر الذي روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول في دعائه: «اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الحور بعد الكور»

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses not returning as not being raised.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه ظن أن لن يحور} [الانشقاق: 14] يقول: يبعث

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as thinking that the person would not return to God.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {إنه ظن أن لن يحور بلى} [الانشقاق: 15] قال: أن لا يرجع إلينا

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r6.claim: Qatada explains it as believing there would be no afterlife or return.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنه ظن أن لن يحور} [الانشقاق: 14] : أن لا معاد له ولا رجعة

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r7.claim: In another report Qatada explains it as thinking he would not be turned back, meaning he would not be resurrected.
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r7.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة {أن لن يحور} [الانشقاق: 14] قال: أن لن ينقلب: يقول: أن لن يبعث

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r8.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r8.anchor: عن سفيان، {ظن أن لن يحور} [الانشقاق: 14] قال: يرجع

TAB-FULL:v24p242/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p242/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses it as turning back or reverting.

TABATABAI:84:7-15/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r10.claim: He thought he would not return to his Lord for accounting and recompense; immersion in sin turns people from the afterlife and makes resurrection seem unlikely.
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r10.anchor: أي لن يرجع والمراد الرجوع إلى ربه للحساب والجزاء، ولا سبب يوجبه عليهم إلا التوغل في الذنوب والآثام الصارفة عن الآخرة

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r8.speaker: الفناري
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r8.claim: Al-Fanārī, in his Tafsīr al-Fātiḥa, says ẓann here means certainty.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r8.anchor: ظن} تيقن كما في "تفسير الفاتحة" للفناري

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r9.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r9.claim: Fatḥ al-Raḥmān takes ẓann in its ordinary sense of supposition, not certainty.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r9.anchor: وقال في "فتح الرحمن" الظن هنا على بابه بمعنى الحسبان لا الظن الذي

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r10.claim: The unbeliever's joy is explained by his supposition that he would never return to God, since he denied resurrection; ḥawr means to return or come back.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r10.anchor: لن يرجع إلى الله تكذيبا للمعاد والحور الرجوع والمحار المرجع

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says he learned the meaning of yaḥūr by hearing a Bedouin woman tell her daughter to return and hearing the expression return to your family.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ما كنت أدري ما معنى يحور حتى سمعت

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r12.claim: The expression seeking refuge from ḥawr after kawr means returning from a good state; a ḥawwārī is a fuller because he restores cloth to whiteness.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r12.anchor: ومنه الحديث نعوذ بالله من الحور بعد الكور أي الرجوع عن حالة جميلة

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r13.claim: Balā affirms the negated proposition: indeed he will certainly return, contrary to his belief.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r13.anchor: {بلى} إيجاب لما بدع لن أي بلى ليحورن البتة وليس الأمر كما يظن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r1.claim: He thought he would not return to the afterlife, meaning he would not be resurrected.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r1.anchor: لن (¬5) يرجع إلى الآخرة (¬6) أي: لن يبعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil explain his thought as believing he would not return to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬7)، ومقاتل (¬8): حسب لا (¬9) يرجع إلى الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r3.claim: Al-ḥawr means return, and al-maḥār means the place of return and final destination.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r4.speaker: لبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites Labīd's phrase يحور رمادا to show ḥawr as returning or turning back.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r4.anchor: وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوءه ... يحور رمادا بعد إذ هو ساطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also cites al-Munaḵḵal al-Yashkurī's ولا تحوري as evidence for the sense “return.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360#2/r5.anchor: وأنشد أيضا للمنحل اليشكري: إذا كنت عاذلتي (¬3) فسيري

QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.claim: He was boastfully pleased among his family with blessings, veiled from their giver, and assumed he would not return to God or live again through resurrection, believing only time governs life and death.
QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.anchor: بطرا في أهله بالنعم محتجبا بها عن المنعم

BURHAN:v4p24/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p24/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p24/r4.claim: A pronoun can belittle its referent, as when Satan is called an evident enemy, when he and his tribe see people unseen, and when the person assumes he will not return.
BURHAN:v4p24/r4.anchor: ومنها التحقير كقوله تعالى ﴿ إنه لكم عدو مبين ﴾

BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.claim: For ten occurrences, many readers and linguists prefer stopping at بلى because it answers the preceding statement without syntactic dependence on what follows; some allow beginning there.
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r1.anchor: أحدها ما يختار فيه كثير من القراء وأهل اللغة الوقف عليها لأنها جواب لما قبلها غير متعلق بما بعدها

ITQAN:v2p354/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p354/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p354/r5.claim: The phrase means that he will not return, described here as an Abyssinian-language gloss; the poet's يحور means returning to ash after brightness.
ITQAN:v2p354/r5.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ أن لن يحور ﴾ قال أن لن يرجع بلغة الحبشة قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك

ITQAN:v2p337#5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p337#5/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p337#5/r1.claim: Lan yaḥūr means he will not be resurrected.

ITQAN:v2p406/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p406/r10.speaker: داود بن هند
ITQAN:v2p406/r10.claim: Dāwūd ibn Hind says yaḥūr means 'returns' in Abyssinian; the same is reported from ʿIkrima.
ITQAN:v2p406/r10.anchor: يحور أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن داود بن هند في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنه ظن أن لن يحور ﴾ قال بلغة الحبشة يرجع

ITQAN:v2p406/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p406/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p406/r11.claim: Al-Suyūṭī notes that the word had already appeared in the questions of Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq to Ibn ʿAbbās.
ITQAN:v2p406/r11.anchor: وتقدم في أسئلة نافع بن الأزرق عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v2p406/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p406/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p406/r20.claim: After years of close research, al-Suyūṭī says he has assembled more than one hundred foreign-origin Qur'anic words, not previously gathered in one book.
ITQAN:v2p406/r20.anchor: فهذا ما وقفت عليه من الألفاظ المعربة في القرآن بعد الفحص الشديد سنين ولم تجتمع قبل في كتاب قبل هذا

ITQAN:v2p406/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p406/r21.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p406/r21.claim: Ibn al-Subkī versified twenty-seven terms, Ibn Ḥajar added twenty-four, and al-Suyūṭī supplied the remaining sixty-odd, bringing the list above one hundred; the cited poem names terms such as Salsabīl, Ṭā Hā, Sijjīl, and Kāfūr.
ITQAN:v2p406/r21.anchor: وقد نظم القاضي تاج الدين بن السبكي منها سبعة وعشرين لفظا في أبيات وذيل عليها الحافظ أبو الفضل بن حجر بأبيات فيها أربعة وعشرون لفظا

ITQAN:v1p215#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r1.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r1.claim: Makki rejects equating the seven famous readers with the hadith’s seven ahruf; that would wrongly exclude other transmitted readings that fit Arabic and the codex script.
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r1.anchor: وقال مكي من ظن أن قراءة هؤلاء القراء كنافع وعاصم هي الأحرف السبعة التي في الحديث فقد غلط غلطا عظيما

ITQAN:v1p215#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r2.claim: Suyuti relays Makki’s history: early authorities listed many readers and regional traditions; around 200 AH the named schools prevailed, while Ibn Mujahid later replaced Yaqub with al-Kisa’i among the seven.
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r2.anchor: كان الناس على رأس المائتين بالبصرة على قراءة أبي عمرو ويعقوب وبالكوفة على قراءة حمزة وعاصم

ITQAN:v1p215#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr’s earlier book chose five readers to match the five codices sent by Uthman; reports of two extra codices to Yemen and Bahrain were unconfirmed, and later substitutions accidentally matched the hadith’s number.
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r3.anchor: وقد صنف ابن جبير المكي قبل ابن مجاهد كتابا في القراءات فاقتصر على خمسة اختار من كل مصر إماما

ITQAN:v1p215#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r4.claim: The seven were selected when readers’ capacity waned, for ease of memorization, from authorities known for trustworthiness, long practice, and broad agreement in transmission.
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r4.anchor: فنظروا إلى من اشتهر بالثقة والأمانة وطول العمر في ملازمة القراءة والاتفاق على الأخذ عنه فأفردوا من كل مصر إماما واحدا

ITQAN:v1p215#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r5.claim: The selection did not discard other transmitted readings: Yaqub, Abu Jaafar, Shayba, and others continued to be transmitted and read.
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r5.anchor: ولم يتركوا مع ذلك نقل ما كان عليه الأئمة غير هؤلاء من القراءات ولا القراءة به كقراءة يعقوب وأبي جعفر وشيبة وغيرهم

ITQAN:v1p215#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r6.claim: The criteria are a sound heard transmission, sound Arabic, and agreement with the codex script; Nafi and Asim have the strongest chains, while Abu Amr and al-Kisa’i are most eloquent.
ITQAN:v1p215#2/r6.anchor: والأصل المعتمد عليه صحة السند في السماع واستقامة الوجه في العربية وموافقة الرسم وأصح القراءات سندا نافع وعاصم وأفصحها أبو عمرو والكسائي

DAMGHANI:v1p311/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p311/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p311/r2.claim: Ẓanna can mean to reckon or suppose: the person thinks he will not return, or that God does not know much of what people do.
DAMGHANI:v1p311/r2.anchor: الثالث ظن يعني حسب قوله في الانشقاق انه ظن ان لن يحور

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r1.claim: Ẓann originally denotes one of two opposing possibilities becoming stronger in the mind; doubt leaves both equal.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r1.anchor: الظن في الأصل : قوة أحد الشيئين على نقيضه في النفس . والفرق بينه وبين الشك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r2.claim: Tazannī is the exercise of conjecture, originally tazannun; ẓanūn means scant in good, maẓinna a place or customary haunt, and ẓinna an accusation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r2.anchor: والتظني : اعمال الظن . والأصل : التظنن . والظنون : القليل الخير . ومظنة الشيء : موضعه ومألفه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r6.claim: A fourth sense is reckoning or supposing; the author glosses the al-Inshiqāq example as ḥasiba.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p424/r6.anchor: والرابع : الحسبان . ومنه قوله تعالى في حم السجدة :

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#5/r1.claim: Yaḥūr means to return and be resurrected.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p521#5/r1.anchor: {إنه ظن أن لن يحور} أي لن يرجع ويبعث.

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r1.claim: أن is the lightened form, like the one at the opening of Surat al-Qiyama, and fills the place of both objects or one object, depending on the grammatical disagreement.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r1.anchor: هذه " أن " المخففة كالتي في أول القيامة، وهي سادة مسد المفعولين أو أحدهما على الخلاف

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r2.claim: حار يحور means to return; Labid's poem uses يحور for turning to ashes after shining.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r2.anchor: و " يحور " معناه يرجع. يقال: حار يحور حورا. قال لبيد: 4526 وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوءه يحور رمادا بعد إذ هو ساطع

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r3.claim: Some grammarians use يحور in the sense of صار, governing a nominative subject and accusative predicate; the cited Labid line supports that analysis, while others parse رمادا as a circumstantial accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r3.anchor: ويستعمل بمعنى صار فيرفع الاسم وينصب الخبر عند بعضهم، وبهذا البيت يستدل قائله

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r4.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r4.claim: Al-Raghib explains the verse's يحور as not returning to life, hence not being resurrected.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب: " الحور التردد: إما بالذات وإما بالفكرة. وقوله تعالى: { إنه ظن أن لن يحور } ، أي: لن يبعث

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r5.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r5.claim: Al-Raghib also describes حور as back-and-forth movement, whether in the entity itself or in thought.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب: " الحور التردد: إما بالذات وإما بالفكرة

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r6.claim: Arabic usage حار الماء في الغدير means the water turns or circulates in a pool.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r6.anchor: وحار الماء في الغدير، تردد فيه

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r7.claim: حار في أمره and تحير mean that someone is perplexed or goes back and forth in a matter.

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r8.claim: المحور is the axle on which a pulley turns, named for its repeated rotation.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r8.anchor: ومنه " المحور " للعود الذي تجري عليه البكرة لتردده

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r9.claim: The saying نعوذ بالله من الحور بعد الكور means seeking refuge from vacillation after firm progress.
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r9.anchor: وقيل: " نعوذ بالله من الحور بعد الكور " ، أي: من التردد في الأمر بعد المضي فيه

SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:84:14/r10.claim: محاورة الكلام means an exchange or return of speech.

ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r7.claim: This describes the disbeliever, who thinks he will not return, meaning he will not be resurrected.
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r7.anchor: هذه صفة الكافر ظن أن لن يحور بأن لن يبعث

ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r8.claim: In Arabic, yaḥūr means to return to God.
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r8.anchor: ومعنى يحور - في اللغة - أن يرجع إلى الله عز وجل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses yaḥūr as returning and adduces Labid's Arabic verse about a radiant person turning to ashes; another report calls the word Abyssinian.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r1.anchor: قال: لن يرجع. قال: وهل كانت العرب تعرف ذلك؟ فقال: نعم، أما سمعت بقول "لبيد بن ربيعة":

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r2.claim: Yaḥūr is the Quran's sole occurrence of this form; the root also yields the dialogue verb in al-Kahf and the verbal noun taḥāwur in al-Mujādilah, alongside other derivatives.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r2.anchor: وحيدة الصيغة في القرآن. ومن المادة، جاء مضارع الرباعي "يحاوره" في آيتي الكهف 34، 37

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses yaḥūr as return and cites Ibn Abbas saying he learned the word from a Bedouin woman telling a girl to return.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p379/r3.anchor: وفسرها "الزمخشري" بـ: لن يرجع. دون أن يشير إلى لغة فيها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r1.claim: Arabic gives the root h-w-r a sense of return, distinct from h-y-r for bewilderment, while related words evoke returning speech, a rotating axle, a trusted helper, echoing air, and circular bright eyes.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r1.anchor: فكان التحاور رجعاً للكلام يتردد بين المتحاورين، والمحور:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r2.claim: Al-Farra interprets the phrase as saying the person will not return to us in the afterlife.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r2.anchor: وفسر الفراء "لن يحور" لن يعود إلينا في الآخرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r3.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains the return as resurrection, judgment, and subsequent reward or punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r3.anchor: وعند القرطبي: لن يرجع مبعوثا فيحاسب ثم يثاب أو يعاقب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r4.claim: Al-Raghib identifies the word's meaning here as resurrection, a specifically Islamic sense fixed by the verse's context.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r4.anchor: وكذلك فسرها "الراغب" في المفردات بالبعث، وهي دلالة إسلامية متعينة في الآية.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r5.speaker: الطوسي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r5.claim: Al-Tusi's explanation that Labid's poetic yaḥūr means become is more fitting for the poem than the afterlife-return sense of the Quranic verse.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p380/r5.anchor: وأما الشاهد الشعري، فأقرب إلى أن يفهم بمعنى يَصير كما قال "الطوسى" في شرح البيت من ديوان لبيد.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r1.claim: Quranic verse endings prioritize meaning over matching letters, though verbal resemblance can align with meaning; departures from a rhyme pattern demonstrate this priority.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r1.anchor: لا يراد بالفاصلة القرآنية مراعاة الحروف وإنما يراد المعنى قبل ذلك ويلتقي الحرف بالمشابهة اللفظية مع المعنى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r4.claim: In 84:14, saying yaḥūrā instead would change the meaning, showing that meaning takes priority over a matching sound ending.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p88/r4.anchor: فلو قال (يحورا) لتغيّر المعنى وفي هذا دلالة على أن القرآن يراعي المعنى قبل مراعاة الناحية اللفظية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r1.claim: Qur’anic verse endings prioritize meaning; sound similarity is accommodated when it fits that meaning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r1.anchor: لا يراد بالفاصلة القرآنية مراعاة الحروف وإنما يراد المعنى قبل ذلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r2.claim: The Qur’an sometimes departs from a sura’s recurring rhyme to preserve meaning, as in Taha and al-Anbiya.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r2.anchor: مغايرة للفاصلة القرآنية في باقي آيات السورة (تزكى، يخشى، هدى) لأن المقصود الأول هو المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r3.claim: Changing the ending to يَحُورا would alter the meaning, so the verse keeps يَحُورَ despite the rhyme pattern.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p538/r3.anchor: فلو قال (يحورا) لتغيّر المعنى وفي هذا دلالة على أن القرآن يراعي المعنى

NASHR:v2p148/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p148/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p148/r7.claim: أن لن is separate wherever it occurs, including 84:14, except that al-Kahf 18:48 and al-Qiyāma 75:3 are joined.
NASHR:v2p148/r7.anchor: (وأن لن) كتب مفصولا حيث وقع نحو: أن لن يقدر، وأن لن يحور إلا في موضعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r3.claim: He thought he would not return to God, denying resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r3.anchor: إنه ظن أن لن يحور: أي أن لن يرجع إلى الله، وهذا تكذيب بالبعث

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r1.speaker: المعترض
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r1.claim: A fifth objection says abrogation evidence concerns the uttered content, not the act of utterance, since some rulings are abrogated while their recitation remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r1.anchor: فلأن الأدلة الدالة على النسخ لا يمكن حملها على التلفظ بل ترجع إلى الملفوظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r2.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes God's speech as the attribute of speaking from speech as what is spoken: the first is one attribute with relations to the many books and words, and is neither actual nor mental letters.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r2.anchor: الحق عز أسمه له كلام بمعنى التكلم وكلام بمعنى المتكلم به وما هو أمر واحد المعنى الأول وهو صفة واحدة تتعدد تعلقاتها بحسب تعدد المتكلم به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r3.claim: The Imam's cited proof says eternal speech has always been command, prohibition, and report; these classify what is spoken, so the unitary attribute with multiple relations is the first sense of speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r3.anchor: نقل الإمام أن الكلام الأزلي لم يزل متصفا بكونه أمرا نهيا خبرا ولا شك أن هذه أقسام المتكلم به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r4.claim: Al-Alusi answers that the sequence objection applies only to actual external wording; mental wording has all its parts together in mental existence while retaining order, so al-Mawaqif can be read consistently.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r4.anchor: إذا أريد من اللفظ الحقيقي وأما إذا أريد النفسي الحكمي فلا ورود له لأن الألفاظ النفسية كلها مجتمعة الأجزاء في الوجود العلمي مع كونها مترتبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r5.claim: He says the third objection assumes that real wording means external speech, but the term may mean inward wording, as the comparison with what exists in a memorizer suggests.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r5.anchor: الإيراد مبني على ظن أن المراد باللفظ الحقيقي مع أنه محتمل لأن يراد النفسي كما يقتضيه ظاهر تشبيهه بالقائم بنفس الحافظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r6.claim: Al-Alusi defines inner speech among the people of truth as the combination of inner wording and meaning, rather than meaning alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r6.anchor: الكلام النفسي عند أهل الحق هو مجموع اللفظ النفسي والمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r7.claim: Al-Alusi explains that al-Mawaqif seems to have understood some Ashʿarīs as making inner speech pure meaning without wording, since they call verbal Quran God's speech only metaphorically.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p13/r7.anchor: ظاهر كلام صاحب المواقف يدل على أنه فهم من ظاهر كلام بعض الأصحاب أن مرادهم بالمعنى هو المقابل للفظ مجردا عن اللفظ مطلقا

DURR-FULL:v8p457/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as thinking he would never be resurrected.
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنه ظن أن لن يحور} قال: لن يبعث

DURR-FULL:v8p457/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r11.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r11.claim: Qatada gives the same interpretation: he thought he would not be raised again.
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r11.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد عن قتادة مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p457/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the phrase as thinking he would not return.
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r12.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس {أن لن يحور} قال: أن لن يرجع

DURR-FULL:v8p457/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r13.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r13.claim: Mujahid says it means he thought he would not return to God.
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r13.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن مجاهد {أن لن يحور} أن لن يرجع إلينا

DURR-FULL:v8p458/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says yaḥūr means return in Abyssinian; the segment gives Labid’s line as Arabic evidence for return.
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r1.anchor: قوله: {أن لن يحور} قال: أن لن يرجع بلغة الحبشة يقول: أن لن يرجع بلغة الحبشة

DURR-FULL:v8p458/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r2.speaker: لبيد
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r2.claim: Labid’s line uses yaḥūr for a bright meteor returning as ashes.
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r2.anchor: أما سمعت قول لبيد: وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوءه يحور رمادا بعد إذ هو ساطع

DURR-FULL:v8p458/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r3.claim: Ikrima says Abyssian usage of “go back to your family” means go to them.
DURR-FULL:v8p458/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة {إنه ظن أن لن يحور} قال: ألم تسمع الحبشي إذا قيل له حر إلى أهلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.claim: Verses 7–15 detail the return to God: right-hand recipients are believers, those given the book behind their backs are polytheists, and the passage divides humanity by its outcome.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.anchor: هذا تفصيل الإجمال الذي في قوله : { إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه } ( الانشقاق : 6 ) أي رجوع جميع الناس أولئك إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r7.claim: The statement that he expected never to return explains why the person handed his book behind his back is destined for the blaze.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r7.anchor: وموقع جملة : { إنه ظن أن لن يحور } موقع التعليل لمضمون جملة : { وأما من أوتي كتابه وراء ظهره } إلى آخرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r8.claim: The person burns in Hell because he believed there would be no return to life after death—that is, he denied resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r8.anchor: فالمعنى : يصلى سعيرا لأنه ظن أن لن يحور ، أي لن يرجع إلى الحياة بعد الموت ، أي لأنه يكذب بالبعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r9.claim: Inna itself supplies the causal force otherwise expressed by a fāʾ of explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r9.anchor: وحرف ( إن ) فيها مغنن عن فاء التعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r10.claim: Ḥāra yaḥūru means to return to one’s former place; it extends metaphorically to returning to a former state after leaving it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r10.anchor: يقال : حار يحور ، إذا رجع إلى المكان الذي كان فيه ، ثم أطلق على الرجوع إلى حالة كان فيها بعد أن فارقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r11.claim: This common metaphor of return also appears in statements that people return to God and that God can restore the human being; resurrection is therefore called the Day of Return.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r1.claim: The emphatic negator لن conveys the denier’s firm certainty that he will not return to life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p225/r1.anchor: الدال على تأكيد النفي وتأييده لحكاية جزمهم وقطعهم بنفيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r1.claim: A Bedouin woman’s حوري to her daughter showed that يحور means return.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r1.anchor: لم أعلم ما معنى يحور، حتى سمعت أعرابية تقول لبنية لها: حوري، أي ارجعي،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r2.claim: ظن retains its ordinary meaning; أن and what follows supply two objects as a light form of إنّ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r2.anchor: والظن هنا على بابه، وأن وما بعدها تسد مسد مفعولي ظن وهي أن المخففة من الثقيلة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r3.claim: Ḥawr means retracing one’s steps; the phrase asks refuge from reversal after increase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r3.anchor: والحور: الرجوع على الأدراج، ومنه: اللهم إني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.claim: God answers that the human will return and nothing is hidden from His sight, issuing a threat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p458/r4.anchor: ثم رد تعالى على ظن هذا الكافر بقوله: بلى، أي يحور ويرجع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatada, and others say he thought he would not return to God after death; ḥawr means return.

JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.claim: Worldly pleasure, limiting one’s aspirations to this life, and turning away from the afterlife are blameworthy and end in regret.
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.anchor: ومنها: أن السرور بأحوال الدنيا وقصر النفس عليها والإعراض عن الآخرة مذموم يعقب الندامة.

MUQATIL:84:10-15/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r4.claim: He thought that God would not resurrect him.
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r4.anchor: يقول: أن لن يبعث الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r10.claim: He thought he would not return alive to be resurrected and called to account, rewarded or punished.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r10.anchor: { إنه ظن أن لن يحور } أي لن يرجع حيا مبعوثا فيحاسب، ثم يثاب أو يعاقب

QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r11.claim: Ḥāra yaḥūru means to return; Labid's verse describes a bright meteor returning to ash after blazing.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r11.anchor: يقال: حار يحور إذا رجع قال لبيد: وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوئه يحور رمادا بعد إذا هو ساطع

QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r12.speaker: عكرمة وداود بن أبي هند
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r12.claim: Ikrima and Dawud ibn Abi Hind say yaḥūru is an Abyssinian word meaning “returns”; the author allows that the two languages may share the same word by derivation.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r12.anchor: وقال عكرمة وداود بن أبي هند، يحور كلمة بالحبشية، ومعناها يرجع

QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r13.claim: The word may also connect with al-khubz al-ḥawārī, bread that returns to whiteness.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r13.anchor: فإنهما كلمة اشتقاق ومنه الخبز الحوارى لأنه يرجع إلى البياض

QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says he learned the meaning from an Arab woman calling her daughter ḥūrī, meaning “come back to me”; ḥawr in Arabic means return.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما كنت أدري: ما يحور؟ حتى سمعت أعرابية تدعو بنية لها: حورى، أي ارجعي إلي
